subject: Biology
description: Causative agents, vectors, vaccines, vitamin-deficiency diseases

questions.explanation: Malaria — caused by Plasmodium (4 main species: P. falciparum — most dangerous; P. vivax — most common in India; P. malariae; P. ovale). Vector: female Anopheles mosquito. Ronald Ross (1897, in India) discovered the parasite's life cycle — Nobel 1902.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: Dengue virus — transmitted by female Aedes aegypti (also spreads chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever). Distinctive black-and-white stripes. Daytime biter. Anopheles — malaria. Tsetse — sleeping sickness (Africa). Sandfly — kala-azar (leishmaniasis).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the VITAMIN DEFICIENCY with its DISEASE. A. Vitamin A.  B. Vitamin B1 (Thiamine).  C. Vitamin C.  D. Vitamin D. List-II: 1. Night blindness.  2. Beri-beri.  3. Scurvy.  4. Rickets.
questions.explanation: Vit A (retinol) — night blindness, xerophthalmia. B1 — beri-beri (cardiac/nervous symptoms). C (ascorbic acid) — scurvy (bleeding gums). D — rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults. B12 — pernicious anaemia.

questions.stem: Which disease is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: TB is caused by the BACTERIUM Mycobacterium tuberculosis — identified by Robert Koch (1882). Influenza (Orthomyxoviridae), AIDS (HIV retrovirus), and chickenpox (Varicella-zoster) are viral. Other bacterial diseases: cholera, typhoid, leprosy, plague, diphtheria, whooping cough.

questions.stem: The BCG vaccine protects primarily against:
questions.explanation: BCG = Bacille Calmette-Guérin — TB vaccine. Developed 1921 by Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin. Polio — OPV (Sabin oral) / IPV (Salk injected). Smallpox eradicated in 1980 (last case 1977 in Somalia). Chickenpox vaccine (varicella) since 1995.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome) is caused by:
questions.explanation: HIV — a retrovirus attacking CD4+ T-cells (helper T-cells). World AIDS Day: 1 December. Transmission: sexual contact, contaminated blood, mother-to-child. Since 1996, ART (antiretroviral therapy) has made HIV a manageable chronic condition.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The disease WIDELY known as 'JAUNDICE' affects which organ primarily?
questions.explanation: Jaundice — yellowing of skin + sclera due to accumulation of bilirubin (from breakdown of haemoglobin). Liver handles bilirubin; liver disease (hepatitis A/B/C/E, gallstones, etc.) → jaundice. Bilirubin levels >2.5 mg/dL → visible jaundice.
